ev.q: CDC analyzed data from the 2018 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS) to estimate past 30-day binge drinking prevalence
The overall unadjusted prevalence of binge drinking during the past 30 days was 16.6%
The age-standardized binge drinking prevalence was higher among men (22.5%) than among women (12.6%)
Median binge drinking frequency and intensity were significantly higher among men (1.9 occasions and 5.9 drinks, respectively)
the median intensity was 5.5 (mean = 7.2) drinks on an occasion
the overall nationwide unadjusted binge drinking prevalence among U.S. adults was 16.6% (95% CI = 16.3%–16.8%)
Binge drinking prevalence was significantly higher among men (22.5%) than among women (12.6%)
Age-standardized prevalence was also estimated by respondents’ sociodemographic characteristics (except prevalence by age group)
BRFSS is an ongoing, state-based, random-digit–dialed, landline and cellular telephone survey
State-level prevalence estimates and 95% CIs were grouped into tertiles to identify geographic patterns.

methods_quotes.q: Unadjusted and age-standardized (to the 2000 U.S. standard population) binge drinking prevalence and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated overall.
were estimated with medians and variances derived using Taylor series linearization.
Statistically significant differences between medians were defined as p<0.05 using pairwise tests and nonoverlapping CIs.
State-level prevalence estimates and 95% CIs were grouped into tertiles to identify geographic patterns.
sampling weights were applied to account for complex sampling design, including nonresponse bias and noncoverage errors
